decisions.reason: The complete GRIS2010 report combines30purposive qualitative interviews with empirical census-based demographic profiles. Current new-survey Results expressly compare descriptive findings to BOTH Gianni2015 and this2010report. A requirement for a statistically tested original hypothesis would wrongly exclude empirical descriptive findings; inability of qualitative interviews to estimate discrimination prevalence does not establish that none of the age/sex/urban/origin profiles is retested. Conversely, the plural comparison does not establish a separate closest-chain finding from2010 beyond the later quantitative2015report and represented Connor/Koenig model. The exact profile/finding allocation and later-report overlap cannot be verified from the unavailable2015empirical chapters, despite the complete2010body and related project report. Retain an actual finding/report-chain ambiguity rather than certifying exclusion from the qualitative design or inventing an extra independent target. Both raw expert exclusions, including the first incorrect interview geography, remain unchanged.

decisions.reason: Lindemann and Stolz (2018) replicate Connor and Koenig's (2015, shipped row 2311) employment-gap mediation model using the 2014 FSO survey (N = 16,487; active labor force N = 11,012; regressions N = 10,916). In Section 5.1 (p. 156, Table 1), after reporting descriptive Muslim versus non-Muslim profiles and 12-month general discrimination (16% vs. 8% in prose; 0.186 vs. 0.079 in Table 1), the authors state that these descriptive findings replicate Gianni et al. (2015) and Gianni, Purdie, Lathion, & Jenny (2010). Gianni et al. (2015; book extract title Les musulmans en Suisse: profils et intégration, vs. reference list Les musulmans de Suisse. Profil et intégration.) reports a distinct 2009 NRP 58 survey of 901 foreign Muslims and 305 non-Muslim Swiss, and Section 3.5 cites it for 12-month religious discrimination among foreign Muslims by origin (21% Turks, 31% North Africans, 15% ex-Yugoslavians). However, only the 5-page book extract and 13-page 2010 NRP 58 project summary are available, while the empirical book chapters (Chapters 3–5) remain unavailable. Without the full empirical chapters, we cannot verify which exact demographic, linguistic, educational, employment, or discrimination tables in Gianni et al. (2015) correspond to Table 1's 2014 active-labor-force comparisons or resolve the denominator differences (all active Muslims vs. foreign origin subgroups, any discrimination vs. religious discrimination).
